units.name: Rysk V12
units.label: curator
units.scope: The currently documented Rysk Premium options vault path explicitly described as running on V12; not every V12 direct RFQ position or the historical pooled/hedged description in the annotation.
spans: The curator defines and runs the strategy; depositors earn volatility income without running the strategy themselves.
The curator selects which options to write and at what strikes and expiries; orders are priced through the RFQ network or agreed OTC and execute onchain.
Rysk Premium runs on Rysk V12, live on HyperEVM mainnet since June 2025
Each position is independent and settled individually, without pooled risk or predefined schedules.
claims: The Premium page assigns option selection and strike/expiry decisions to a curator who operates the strategy for depositors.
The same page places Premium on V12. The separate V12 solution page describes independent positions, so a vault-specific role should not be generalized to every V12 trade.

Users of that documented Premium vault path rely on a named strategy-selection role, satisfying R-curator for this scoped path. This does not validate the annotation's delta-hedging account or establish historical equivalence.
limits: Two retained bodies belong to the same official publisher family and are not independent corroboration.
A live documentation snapshot has no immutable product commit; the Premium launch/version assertion is a publisher statement, not independently verified chain state.
No vault manager address, specific mandate, historical epoch policy, dynamic hedging implementation or actual trade was verified.
The V12 no-pooled-risk description and current Premium vault description apply to different documented user paths; neither is silently used to rewrite the other.
Zero-valued dynamic site counters and marketing claims about safety/audits were not used as evidence.
units.next: Independently review the Premium/V12-scoped curator finding and split or qualify the historical unit boundary if needed before an accepted overlay. Retrieve a particular vault's role and mandate only in a separately bounded follow-up.

units.name: Tether USDT
units.label: async_cross_domain
units.scope: Issuer-coordinated exchange chain swaps described in the retained Tether article dated October24,2019, as served at capture time; not an autonomous bridge or every USDT transfer.
spans: After confirming receipt of these funds in our treasury wallet on the initial blockchain, the same amount of funds will be sent on the destination blockchain back to the other exchange.
The entire process of the chain swap is coordinated and managed with the other exchange until completion.

After this transfer is completed, we either burn the same amount of USD₮ tokens on the initial blockchain or retain these tokens in our treasury wallet on the initial blockchain to be used for future chain swaps with our clients.
claims: Tether describes receipt confirmation on an originating chain before the corresponding transfer on a destination chain, coordinated with the requesting exchange.

This is a causally linked two-domain workflow with an explicit receipt-confirmation delivery boundary, satisfying R-async_cross_domain for the issuer-coordinated chain-swap path. Multichain token availability alone was not the reason.
Source-chain destruction is conditional: the article also permits retaining inventory after destination delivery. The finding does not assume a universal atomic burn-and-mint mechanism.
limits: The two tether.to HTTP200 bodies were meta-refresh wrappers with no article text; they receive zero substantive evidence credit. The explicitly named tether.io destination was followed without executing embedded scripts.
Three response bodies were retained including those two wrappers, within the cap; only one is a substantive primary article.
The displayed article date is historical but the served bytes are a current capture, not a recovered2019 snapshot.
Receipt confirmation is the documented boundary; no block threshold, finality proof, latency bound, relayer code, cryptographic cross-chain verification or live swap transaction was inspected.
No claim is made about current chain support, reserve sufficiency, guaranteed redemption, or equivalence to USDT0/LayerZero and other separate products.
units.next: Independently review the issuer-mediated workflow finding. Any stronger execution or historical assertion requires separately binding the actual chain pair, confirmation policy and transaction sequence.

units.name: Kalshi
units.label: exchange
units.scope: Currently documented Kalshi event-market orderbook and V2 order submission, as captured; no particular listed market, executed trade or clearing-law conclusion.
spans: Endpoint for submitting event-market orders using the V2 request/response shape
cancels the resting maker order and continues matching
endpoint returns the current state of bids for a specific market.
claims: The V2 interface submits event-market orders, defines buy and sell sides and describes matching against resting maker orders. A separate endpoint exposes market bids.
These interfaces describe direct trading of event contracts through an orderbook, satisfying R-exchange beyond merely issuing or resolving a prediction claim.
limits: The retained sources are two pages from one official API publisher, not independent corroboration.
Current V2 single-book/fixed-point documentation is not asserted to equal the historical API underlying the original annotation.
No authenticated request, order placement, live orderbook sample, trade, price, payment or market outcome was executed or inspected.
Exchange as an economic-function label does not establish any particular regulatory registration, central-counterparty obligation, custody arrangement, collateral rule or onchain deployment.
units.next: Independently review the event-market orderbook-scoped exchange finding; preserve prediction as the existing separate facet label and leave clearing/legal claims outside this packet.

units.name: Polymarket
units.label: exchange
units.scope: Currently documented CLOB V2 event-token trading path and its order lifecycle, as captured; not a verification of V1 historical contract bytes or live V2 settlement.
spans: Orders are created offchain, matched by an operator, and settled onchain through smart contracts.
Transfers tokens from seller to buyer
Transfers pUSD from buyer to seller
CLOB V2 is live as of April 28, 2026.
Legacy V1 SDKs and V1-signed orders are no longer supported on production.
claims: The order lifecycle describes matching signed orders and reciprocal delivery of event tokens and pUSD between seller and buyer.
The documented matched trade and reciprocal settlement directly enable exchange of instruments, satisfying R-exchange independently of event-claim issuance or resolution.

The migration page identifies V2 and distinguishes unsupported V1 orders. This packet therefore scopes its finding to the current documented V2 path rather than silently equating it to the original unresolved deployment.
limits: Two pages from one official documentation publisher are not independent corroboration.
Publisher claims about noncustodial or atomic settlement were not verified by contract execution or a Lean refinement.
No SDK code was run, wallet connected, signature made, order placed or contract address matched to deployed bytecode.
The pUSD/V2 terminology is recorded as version context; no claim about its reserve quality, collateral equivalence, current fees or access eligibility is made.
The exchange finding does not adjudicate oracle/dispute, custody, regulatory or async cross-domain labels.
units.next: Independently review the CLOB V2 exchange finding. Bind the historical product/deployment separately before extrapolating from this current documentation capture.

units.name: Grove Finance (Onchain Capital Allocator)
units.label: fund_share
units.scope: Grove's documented allocation into the Janus Henderson Anemoy JAAA fund and the issuer's public product description; Grove capital-provider rights and precise proportional share rights remain unbound.
spans: Grove’s first major deployment is a $1 billion allocation into the Janus Henderson Anemoy JAAA Fund, a fully tokenized vehicle that holds only AAA-rated CLO tranches.
It is real exposure to the top of the CLO capital stack, represented by onchain tokens that inherit the economic rights of fully compliant, real-world securities.
through an actively managed portfolio of AAA-rated CLO tranches.
Regulated open-ended BVI fund for non-US professional investors
claims: Grove describes an allocation into tokenized JAAA and economic exposure through tokens; Anemoy describes a managed CLO portfolio, fund structure and subscriptions/redemptions.

These retained public descriptions do not specify the proportional beneficial/economic share right required by R-fund_share for the instrument being classified, nor bind Grove capital-provider claims to that right. A managed-fund name and an investment allocation alone do not close this predicate.

The underlying JAAA investment and a direct instrument offered by Grove must remain distinct. Proposed not_evidenced records this bounded rights/scope gap; it does not deny that JAAA or another Grove exposure can carry fund-share rights.
limits: Two substantive primary bodies were retained: Grove's article and Anemoy's fund page. Their commercial relationship means different hostnames alone do not establish independent corroboration.

The Grove body carries article content in JSON-encoded React flight data; literal data were decoded for inspection without executing scripts. The initially empty visible-main extraction is retained and is not falsely described as missing source content.

The retained Anemoy page records its own publication metadata. Neither body establishes the precise historical offering documents, share class, token/share ratio, register of members or Grove depositor interface.

A secondary governance discussion discovered possible offering-document details but no primary governing instrument was recovered from it; those secondary assertions are not adjudication evidence here.

The tokenized Anemoy JAAA fund is not silently equated with the US-listed JAAA ETF or with underlying CLO tranches. No legal guarantee, bankruptcy-remoteness claim, NAV accuracy, redemption timing or live balance was verified.
units.next: Retrieve issuer-authored governing share/portfolio terms and bind the exact instrument boundary—Grove's held asset versus a claim issued to its capital provider—before proposing a proportional fund_share finding. Keep this packet unresolved meanwhile.
